records.literal_gloss: For everything [there is] an appointed time, and a time for every matter under the heavens.

en.L: For everything [there is] an appointed time, \q and a time for every matter under the heavens:
en.B: There is a set time for everything, \q a time for every matter under the heavens:
en.R: Everything has its own time. \q There is a time for every activity in this world:

es.L: Para todo [hay] un tiempo señalado, \q y un tiempo para cada asunto bajo los cielos:
es.B: Hay un momento fijado para todo, \q un tiempo para cada asunto bajo los cielos:
es.R: Cada cosa tiene su momento. \q Toda actividad en este mundo tiene su tiempo:

fr.L: Pour toute chose [il y a] un moment fixé, \q et un temps pour chaque affaire sous les cieux :
fr.B: Chaque chose a son moment fixé, \q chaque affaire sous les cieux a son temps :
fr.R: Chaque chose arrive en son temps. \q Toute activité en ce monde a son moment :

sw.L: Kwa kila kitu [kuna] wakati uliowekwa, \q na wakati kwa kila jambo chini ya mbingu:
sw.B: Kila kitu kina wakati wake uliopangwa, \q kila jambo chini ya mbingu lina wakati wake:
sw.R: Kila kitu kina wakati wake. \q Kila shughuli katika ulimwengu huu ina wakati wake:

vi.L: Mọi việc đều [có] một thời được định, \q và một lúc cho mỗi việc dưới các tầng trời:
vi.B: Mọi sự đều có thời điểm đã định, \q mỗi việc dưới trời đều có lúc của nó:
vi.R: Việc gì cũng có thời điểm của nó. \q Mọi việc trong đời này đều có lúc:

ko.L: 모든 것에 정해진 때가 [있고], \q 하늘 아래 모든 일에 때가 있으니,
ko.B: 무엇에든 정해진 시기가 있고, \q 하늘 아래 모든 일에는 그 때가 있으니,
ko.R: 무엇이든 그 일이 있을 때가 따로 있다. \q 이 세상의 모든 일에는 알맞은 때가 있다.

pt.L: Para tudo [há] um tempo marcado, \q e um tempo para cada assunto debaixo dos céus:
pt.B: Há um momento fixado para tudo, \q uma hora para cada coisa debaixo dos céus:
pt.R: Cada coisa tem o seu tempo. \q Há um tempo para cada atividade neste mundo:

am.L: ለሁሉም ነገር የተወሰነ ጊዜ [አለው]፤ \q ከሰማያትም በታች ላለ ጉዳይ ሁሉ ጊዜ [አለው]፦
am.B: ለሁሉም ነገር የተወሰነ ጊዜ አለ፤ \q ከሰማይ በታች ለሚደረግ ጉዳይ ሁሉ ጊዜ አለ፦
am.R: ሁሉም ነገር የራሱ ጊዜ አለው። \q በዚህ ዓለም ለሚደረግ ተግባር ሁሉ ጊዜ አለ፦

hi.L: हर चीज़ के लिए एक ठहराया हुआ समय [है], \q और आकाश के नीचे हर काम के लिए एक समय:
hi.B: हर चीज़ के लिए एक तय समय है, \q आकाश के नीचे हर काम के लिए एक समय:
hi.R: हर चीज़ का अपना समय होता है। \q आकाश के नीचे हर काम के लिए एक समय है:

ru.L: Для всего [есть] назначенный срок, \q и время для всякого дела под небесами:
ru.B: Всему есть установленный срок, \q время для всякого дела под небесами:
ru.R: Всё происходит в своё время. \q Есть время для каждого дела под небом:

ja.L: すべてのものに定まった時があり、 \q 天の下のあらゆる事柄に時がある。
ja.B: 何にでも定められた時がある。 \q 天の下のどんな営みにも、それにふさわしい時がある。
ja.R: どんなことにも、それぞれの時がある。 \q この世でするすべてのことに、時がある。

decisions.choice: verses 1-8: a poem of times
decisions.reason: After the heading line, fourteen pairs of opposites follow, from birth and death (verse 2) to war and peace (verse 8). Each pair is set in a balanced line, and the poem is set in lines; the rest of the chapter is reflective prose.

decisions.choice: appointed time: a fixed or set time
decisions.reason: The word (zeman) is a later Hebrew word for a set time or date (Nehemiah 2:6; Esther 9:27).

decisions.choice: time: the right moment or occasion for something
decisions.reason: The word ('et) is a time that fits what happens in it. It is said twenty-eight times in verses 2-8. Verse 11 says that God has made everything fitting in its time; verse 14 that what God does lasts. People live within times they do not set.

decisions.choice: matter: an activity or affair
decisions.reason: The word (chefets) first means delight or desire; in this book it means any matter or business people take up (3:17; 5:7; 8:6).

decisions.choice: in this world
decisions.reason: Readable's wording for "under the heavens" and "under the sun" (see 1:3, 1:13).

decisions.choice: a colon at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The list of times that follows hangs on this line, so each level closes it with a colon and sets the pairs of verses 2-8 as one list.

decisions.choice: "tiempo señalado ... tiempo" (L); "momento ... tiempo" (B, R); the pairs "tiempo de ..." (L), "un tiempo para ..." (B, R)
alternatives: "Todo tiene su tiempo, y todo lo que se quiere debajo del cielo tiene su hora"
decisions.reason: The poem is drafted fresh from the Hebrew: two words for time in the heading (m2, m3), then "tiempo" for 'et in every pair, twenty-eight times, as the Hebrew repeats one word. The familiar Reina-Valera wording is not followed.

decisions.choice: « moment fixé ... temps » (L, B); « un temps pour ... » in the pairs (L, B); « un moment pour ... » (R)
alternatives: « Il y a un temps pour tout, un temps pour toute chose sous les cieux »
decisions.reason: The poem is drafted fresh from the Hebrew: two words for time in the heading (m2, m3), then one word repeated in every pair, as the Hebrew repeats 'et. Readable uses the everyday « moment ». The familiar Segond wording is not followed.

decisions.choice: "wakati uliowekwa ... wakati" (L); "wakati wa ..." in every pair
decisions.reason: The poem is drafted fresh from the Hebrew, with one word, "wakati", repeated in every pair as the Hebrew repeats 'et (m3). The familiar Union Version wording is not followed.

decisions.choice: "thời ... lúc" (L); "thời điểm ... lúc" (B, R); "lúc" in every pair
alternatives: "kỳ" ("có kỳ sanh ra, và có kỳ chết")
decisions.reason: The poem is drafted fresh from the Hebrew. "lúc", the everyday word for a moment or occasion, is repeated in every pair as the Hebrew repeats 'et (m3); the 1925 version's "kỳ" is not used.

decisions.choice: the heading ends "때가 있으니," (L, B), and the list of verses 2-8 closes in verse 8
decisions.reason: Korean has no colon to hang a list on, so at Literal and Balanced the heading runs on into the pairs, which close with "때이다" in verse 8; Readable closes the heading and makes verses 2-8 the subject of "때가 있다" in verse 8. Both familiar Korean wordings are avoided; the poem is drafted fresh from the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: 'et: "um tempo para ... e um tempo para ..." (L, R); "hora de ..., hora de ..." (B)
decisions.reason: The poem of verses 2-8 is among the best-known passages in Portuguese Bibles, and the familiar wording pulls hard. Literal says "um tempo para" with the verb, as the English Literal shows the Hebrew form; Balanced says "hora", the Portuguese word for the right moment ("chegou a hora", m3), and sets the halves side by side without "e", as the English Balanced does; Readable says "um tempo para" with plain words. The lines break where the English breaks them.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The English capitalises pronouns for God as a reader setting. The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change in Amharic and the text has no span. This holds through the chapter.

decisions.choice: "የተወሰነ ጊዜ" (appointed time) and "ጊዜ" (time)
decisions.reason: zeman is a set time and ʿet the right moment; "የተወሰነ ጊዜ" and "ጊዜ" keep the two apart, and "ጊዜ" alone then carries the whole poem. The familiar wording of the opening line is avoided.

decisions.choice: the pairs of verses 2-8: "... के लिए एक समय और ... के लिए एक समय" (Literal); "एक समय ... का, एक समय ... का" (Balanced); "एक समय है ... का और एक समय है ... का" (Readable)
alternatives: "... का समय, और ... का भी समय"
decisions.reason: The poem of times (m1) is drafted from the Hebrew and its gloss, with one pattern per level, so that it does not follow the wording of older Hindi Bibles. Literal renders each Hebrew "to" with a verb as "... के लिए" and keeps the Hebrew "and" between the halves of a pair; Balanced sets the halves side by side without "and", as the English Balanced does; Readable says each half as a short plain statement with "है". The list hangs on this verse, which ends with a colon at every level, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "ठहराया हुआ समय" (L); "तय समय" (B)
decisions.reason: The first word is a fixed or set time (m2); Literal and Balanced say so. "Under the heavens" is "आकाश के नीचे" at every level (see 1:3).

decisions.choice: a colon at the end of the verse, each pair of times in lines
decisions.reason: The list of times that follows hangs on this line, so each level closes it with a colon and sets the pairs of verses 2-8 in lines, as the English does (m1). The poem is drafted from the Hebrew, not from the familiar Synodal list: Literal pairs imperfective infinitives with и, Balanced sets perfective infinitives side by side without и, Readable uses everyday words and nouns where they read simply.

decisions.choice: The poem of times (3:2-8): "Xするのに時があり、Yするのに時がある、" (L), "Xする時もあれば、Yする時もある。" (B), "Xする時があり、Yする時がある。" (R), one pair to a \q line as in the English
alternatives: 生まれる時、死ぬ時 (bare noun list)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "a time to (do)" with のに; Balanced pairs each line with もあれば…もある, a natural way to set two opposites side by side; Readable keeps the plainest form. The well-known Japanese versions of this poem are avoided, as the brief asks.

am.L: የመውለድ ጊዜ፣ የመሞትም ጊዜ፤ \q የመትከል ጊዜ፣ የተተከለውንም የመንቀል ጊዜ፤

hi.L: जन्म देने के लिए एक समय और मरने के लिए एक समय, \q रोपने के लिए एक समय और रोपे हुए को उखाड़ने के लिए एक समय;
hi.B: एक समय जन्म देने का, एक समय मरने का, \q एक समय पौधे लगाने का, एक समय लगाए हुए को जड़ से उखाड़ने का,

ru.B: время родить, время умереть, \q время посадить, время вырвать посаженное,
ru.R: время для рождения и время для смерти, \q время сажать растения и время их выдёргивать,

ja.L: 産むのに時があり、死ぬのに時がある、 \q 植えるのに時があり、植えたものを抜くのに時がある、
ja.B: 産む時もあれば、死ぬ時もある。 \q 植える時もあれば、植えたものを抜く時もある。
ja.R: 生まれる時があり、死ぬ時がある。 \q 植える時があり、植えた物を引き抜く時がある。

decisions.choice: to give birth: the start of a life
decisions.reason: The verb (yalad) is active, "to bear a child". Set beside "to die", it stands for the start of life as death stands for its end; many render it "to be born".

decisions.choice: birth and death first: the two times no one chooses
decisions.reason: The list opens with the beginning and end of life, which no person sets for themselves, and the second pair takes the same shape in the life of plants.

decisions.choice: a time for giving birth and a time for dying
alternatives: a time to give birth and a time to die
decisions.reason: Through verses 2-7 Literal renders each Hebrew "to" with a verb (le- with the infinitive) as "for ...ing", which shows the form and keeps the Hebrew "and" between the two halves of each pair.

decisions.choice: a time to give birth, a time to die
alternatives: a time to give birth and a time to die
decisions.reason: Through verses 2-8 Balanced sets the two halves of each pair side by side without "and", as English lists often do; the Hebrew joins them with "and", which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: a time for birth and a time for death
alternatives: a time to bear and a time to die
decisions.reason: Readable uses nouns for the first pair, which reads simply; it says the same (m1).

decisions.choice: um tempo para nascer
decisions.reason: The English Readable uses nouns for the first pair; Portuguese reads more simply with the verbs "nascer" and "morrer", which say the same (m1).

decisions.choice: each line a pair of nouns, "የX ጊዜ፣ የY(ም) ጊዜ" (L, B); "የX ጊዜና የY ጊዜ" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lines are bare noun phrases, "a time of X and a time of Y", with no verb. Amharic keeps that shape with the verbal noun in a genitive ("የመውለድ ጊዜ"), drafted fresh rather than in the familiar "ለ... ጊዜ አለው" pattern. Literal keeps the Hebrew "and" as -ም; Balanced drops it as the English Balanced does; Readable joins each pair with -ና. The shape holds through verse 8.

decisions.choice: "የመውለድ ጊዜ" (giving birth, L, B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is active, to bear a child, as the English Literal and Balanced have it; Readable says "የልደት ጊዜ" (a time for birth), as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "जन्म", "मौत"
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, Readable uses nouns for the first pair, which reads simply; it says the same (m1).

decisions.choice: время родить, время умереть
decisions.reason: Through verses 2-8 Balanced sets the two halves of each pair side by side without и, as the English Balanced does, and uses perfective infinitives, each time a single act.

decisions.choice: рожать
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is active, to bear a child (m1); Literal keeps it, where a familiar rendering says "to be born".

decisions.choice: throwing away and gathering stones: the meaning is uncertain
alternatives: clearing a field of stones, and gathering stones to build
spoiling an enemy's field with stones (2 Kings 3:19, 25)
a picture of sexual relations, matching the next line
decisions.reason: The pair is not explained. Farmers cleared stones from fields (Isaiah 5:2) and gathered stones to build walls and houses; an army could ruin a field by throwing stones on it (2 Kings 3:19, 25). Some early Jewish interpreters read it as a picture of a husband and wife coming together or keeping apart, which would match the embracing of the next line. The text does not say which is meant.

decisions.reason: The verb (chavaq) is used of a loving embrace (Song 2:6) and of greeting (Genesis 29:13). The second half is literally "a time to be far from embracing".

decisions.reason: What throwing away and gathering stones meant is uncertain (m1): clearing a field, building, or a figure for something else. Every level keeps the plain words and adds no explanation.

decisions.choice: gain: what is left over (see 1:3)
decisions.reason: The word (yitron) is the book's word for lasting gain.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: gain ... hard work (B); what good ... hard work (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for yitron and 'amal (see 1:3).

decisions.choice: "labuta", with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs the setting for "they toil|he toils"; the Portuguese verb has no pronoun and no gender, so no span is needed (see 2:14).

decisions.choice: no gender span where the English has one: the Amharic wording already covers men and women
alternatives: a span with a masculine alternative
decisions.reason: Amharic "ሰው", "ሰዎች" and the generic masculine verb already include men and women, so there is only one wording and no span. This holds through the chapter.

decisions.choice: no gender span on "वह"
decisions.reason: Hindi "वह" and the generic verb are ordinary for anyone, so the English span has nothing to change (see 1:3).

decisions.choice: выгода (L, B), толк (R); труд, тяжкий труд, тяжёлая работа
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for yitron and 'amal (see 1:3); the question of 1:3 again (m1).

decisions.choice: работающий ... он, no gender span
decisions.reason: Russian работающий and человек stand for anyone, and their pronouns follow the noun's grammar, so where the English Literal has gender spans for a single person Russian has one wording. This holds for the whole chapter; children of humankind keeps its span.
